title: Defenders of the Last Stand - Take a Look
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oUdstwXRu2c

Daniel (@dungeondive) looks at Defenders of the Last Stand, Richard Launius and Jason Maxwell's post-apocalyptic co-op, and uses it to trace a lineage he clearly feels affection for. Arkham Horror 2nd Edition pulled him back into hobby gaming after a five-year break and set his expectations for what a modern adventure game should be; Matt Leacock stripped that idea to its essentials with Pandemic; Launius took it back into fantasy with Defenders of the Realm, which Daniel found thematically thin.

Last Stand, he argues, is Defenders of the Realm advanced — and crucially, the theme is no longer pasted on. You play Rangers in the American southwest holding back four factions and their leaders, each advancing along a path toward the last human city. Let a leader in, or four raiders, and it's over. On your turn you spend action tokens adventuring, gambling, healing, scavenging artifacts or sabotaging leaders; then the threat deck pushes the world forward.

His caveats are real: a lot of fiddly rule exceptions that are hard to hold solo, a game that runs long, and a rulebook whose contents are all present but badly structured. He recommends a fan-made manual and three players.

----

Daniel traces a straight line from Arkham Horror through Pandemic to this — does the threat-management formula still have room to grow, or has it said everything it has to say?
